card.pass_when: All intended connections are routed; saved-state connectivity, return paths and relevant checks inspected on the current revision.
card.task: Start from the latest incoming graph record and its evidence to define this visit. On a review return, first inspect its findings without editing copper: separate accepted geometry and checker artifacts, repair checker defects, and bring conflicting rules or owner tradeoffs to the owner with a recommendation and cost. Define the next bounded copper batch and plan each task file's `Mode:` (`ipc` for clean channels/buses, `hybrid` default for mixed runs, `interactive` for dense Push-and-Shove) only after those dispositions and owner authorization. Work in the KiCad machine's editor. Commit task files with the named connections and `Mode:`. Use the Tool command in this brief. It runs the locked KiCad editor, verifies the saved board and records the result. Before a copper batch, its nets must be clear of open issues. That run is the only way copper is laid: never write tracks, vias or pours with ad-hoc scripts (`wrapper_calls`), raw `create_items` outside `kicad_lay.py`, direct `.kicad_pcb` edits, or an unauthorized router, and never lay copper by hand outside the run. When the run cannot lay a connection, record needs_lead with what the tool returned and stop; the card refuses pass and more_work while the board holds copper that no run committed. Refill zones and save. Run the copper diff against origin/main with the batch nets, declaring each change to earlier copper or part positions as a fix with its reason. Render and inspect the pictures. Run fresh saved-fill, DRC/parity, route-quality, electrical, pad-mask, thermal-relief, hand-solder-joint and exhaustive checks and the relevant track-craft checks. Resolve or explain each finding and obtain the targeted board critic. Record more_work with the batch nets until the whole board is routed. Preserve accepted placements, labels and waivers unless the owner changes that decision.
